The test image shows **split-open soybean pods** held in hand. Key observations:
- Mature/dried pods split to show seeds inside
- Seeds show brown-black discoloration and shriveling
- One seed has dark mottling/blotches
- Pod walls have brownish staining

This points to seed/pod disease. Top candidates: **Diaporthe**, **Phomopsis**, **Anthracnose**. Let me view reference images.
The Phomopsis reference shows pod lesions with pycnidia spots. The Anthracnose shows dark pod lesions. Let me check more candidates.
Charcoal_Rot, Fusarium, Cercospora, and Septoria are stem/root/leaf diseases — ruled out. The test image is clearly about **pod/seed disease**. Let me check a few more candidates.

I've now viewed 12 reference images. Let me consolidate my analysis.

**Test image analysis:**
- Split soybean pods held in hand
- Seeds inside: one yellow/normal, one brown with dark mottling, one shrunken/aborted with dark border
- Mature, dried pod appearance
- Damage is specifically **inside the pod** — seed discoloration and decay

**Ruling out:**
- Diaporthe: stem canker symptoms, not pod/seed
- Charcoal_Rot/Fusarium: root/stem diseases
- Bacterial_Blight/Soybean_rust/Frogeye/Cercospora/Septoria: leaf diseases
- White_Mold: white mycelium on stems/pods
- Purple_Seed_Stain: purple/violet seed coloration (not brownish-black)

**Best match — Phomopsis:** The Phomopsis reference shows pod and stem blight with characteristic pod lesions. Phomopsis longicolla causes seed decay where seeds become shrunken and brown-black inside pods — precisely what is visible in the test image (split pods showing diseased seeds with dark discoloration and shriveling).

One seed is aborted/shrunken with a dark margin, another shows dark mottled spots on a brown background. This seed-decay pattern inside mature dried pods closely matches the Phomopsis reference which focuses on pod and stem blight. Other pod/seed diseases (Anthracnose shows external pod surface lesions, Purple_Seed_Stain shows purple coloration) do not match as well."}
